subject: English
passage: In varieties of Spanish spoken in northern Mexico, speakers frequently use the diminutive suffix "-ito" or "-ita" even when referring to objects that are not particularly small (as in "casita" for any house or "perrito" for any dog). Spanish dialects of New Mexico and southern Colorado show similar patterns of diminutive usage, applying these suffixes broadly beyond their original size-related meanings. Historical records indicate that these southwestern US regions were settled primarily by families migrating from northern Mexico in the 18th and 19th centuries. Thus, linguists have concluded that ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: distinctive use of diminutive suffixes will eventually spread from Spanish dialects in the southwestern US to dialects spoken in other regions.
choices.B: the Spanish dialects spoken in northern Mexico were influenced by dialects spoken in New Mexico and southern Colorado.
choices.C: the Spanish dialects spoken in New Mexico and southern Colorado acquired their distinctive use of diminutive suffixes from dialects spoken in northern Mexico.
choices.D: families from northern Mexico abandoned their distinctive use of diminutive suffixes after relocating to the southwestern United States.

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer because it most logically completes the text's discussion of Spanish dialects spoken in northern Mexico and the southwestern United States. The text indicates that these dialects share a feature: using diminutive suffixes broadly beyond their typical size-related meanings. The text goes on to state that records indicate the southwestern US regions were settled primarily by families from northern Mexico. It is reasonable to assume that the Spanish dialects spoken by these settlers were influenced by the Spanish dialects spoken in their homeland of northern Mexico. It follows, then, that the distinctive use of diminutive suffixes in northern Mexican dialects carried over into the southwestern US dialects as they developed—that is, that the southwestern US dialects likely acquired this feature from dialects spoken in northern Mexico.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect because the text suggests that northern Mexican ancestry explains the origin of distinctive diminutive usage in Spanish dialects spoken in the southwestern US, since that linguistic feature is also found in northern Mexican dialects; the text doesn't address any other dialects or suggest that the feature will spread elsewhere.
